utility.notes: The City of Irvine's own official 'Local Utility Companies' page identifies Southern California Edison as the electric utility serving Irvine, noting SCE continues to handle delivery, billing, and line maintenance even after Orange County Power Authority (OCPA) began providing generation service.

value.name: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA)
value.notes: Irvine residents were automatically enrolled in Orange County Power Authority (OCPA), a CCA, for generation as of October 2022, per the City of Irvine's own materials. SCE remains the interconnection/distribution/billing utility.

permit_authority.notes: Directly fetched and confirmed from the city's own official page.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — this is a utility-wide fact (the same URL applies to every city in SCE's distribution territory, including Irvine), not city-specific. sce.com returned a DNS-level failure to automated fetch; the URL is confirmed to exist under this exact title on SCE's own domain via search engine indexing.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. This tier is explicitly available to both PG&E and SCE residential customers per the statewide SGIP administrator; SCE administers it within its own distribution territory, which includes Irvine/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for the PG&E-territory pilot records, applied here for the first time to an SCE-administered territory — the general-market tier's own eligibility text already explicitly names both PG&E and SCE customers, so this is a direct textual match, not an assumption. Confidence set slightly below the PG&E-territory records (0.6 vs 0.65) since SCE's specific administrator role for Irvine has not been independently re-confirmed the way PG&E's was for Bay Area cities. 'Available through 2025' read as expiring 2025-12-31, before last_verified, hence 'expired'; the other tier's status is 'unknown'. Removed the previously-listed "SGIP - Equity Resiliency" line item on 2026-08-09: its expires_on (2025-12-31) has definitively elapsed and no renewal/replacement was confirmed this session, so it no longer represents a current program; the remaining item(s) here are still active/unknown-status per their own status field.

required_documents.notes: From the City of Irvine's 'Adding a Rooftop Solar Energy System' page — appears to be the standard residential submittal package rather than the separate 10kW-or-less expedited electronic-submittal pathway's own (shorter) checklist, which was not independently located this session.

inspection_steps.notes: Not confirmed this session — the fetched page did not detail a specific inspection-scheduling procedure.

value.notes: The City of Irvine's own page states: 'Standard review for single family residential projects are 5 working days. More complex projects may take two weeks.' Recorded as 5-10 working days (2 weeks read as 10 working days). Separately, the city also offers an expedited electronic-submittal pathway for systems 10 kW or less, and (per independent reporting, not confirmed on this page) a same-day 'PermitsDIRECT!' option via a third-party platform for systems up to 38.4 kW with at most one battery storage system — timeline for those expedited pathways was not independently confirmed on the city's own page this session, so only the standard-review timeline is recorded here.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited Electronic Submittal (residential solar systems 10 kW or less)
other_conditions: Must comply with the city's adopted building and fire codes, zoning ordinance (Chapter 3-31), and homeowner association approval where applicable
Separate application pathways exist for single-family residential vs. commercial/multi-family properties

Independent reporting (not confirmed directly on the city's own fetched page) describes a separate same-day 'PermitsDIRECT!' (Symbium) pathway for rooftop solar+battery systems up to 38.4 kW with at most one battery storage system — not included in the structured fields above since it wasn't independently confirmed on an official city page this session
